writing.prompt: Explain the difference between “probability an offspring is an affected son” and “probability a son is affected.” Use a carrier mother and unaffected father.
writing.model: For XAXa × XAY, one of four total offspring combinations is an affected son, so the joint probability is 1/4. Among the two son combinations, one is affected, giving a conditional probability of 1/2. The denominator differs.

writing.prompt: Explain why an affected father does not directly pass an X-linked allele to his sons in the typical XX/XY model.
writing.model: Sons receive the father’s Y chromosome, not his X. The paternal X goes to daughters. Therefore direct father-to-son transmission does not occur through an X-linked locus in this model.

videos.title: Sex-linked inheritance — video support
videos.purpose: Use a typical XX/XY model to solve X-linked crosses and distinguish conditional from joint probabilities.
videos.fallback: Consider XBXb × XBY. The four equally likely combinations are XBXB, XBXb, XBY and XbY. One of four children is expected to be affected. Among sons only, one of two is expected to be affected. The probability of “a son who is affected” is 1/4 among all children. The probability that “the next son is affected” is 1/2 conditional on being a son. The wording changes the denominator, not the biological cross. An affected father passes his X chromosome to daughters and his Y to sons in this model. Father-to-son transmission therefore is not expected for an X-linked allele through that direct chromosome path.

worked.title: Answer two similar-looking questions
worked.scenario: A carrier XAXa mother and unaffected XAY father have children in a simple X-linked recessive model.
steps: List the four equally likely combinations: XAXA, XAXa, XAY and XaY.
Affected child: XaY is one of four, so probability = 1/4.
Affected among sons: XaY is one of two son outcomes, so probability = 1/2.
A son who is affected among all children: probability remains 1/4.
Write the denominator in words to show which question you answered.
